teacher: Native two-turn reply-search-256/8/64 self-play, positions sampled every fourth round
method: Read the already-collected candidate action sequences and selected slate indices. Count selected turn lengths and whether a nonstatic teacher-selected turn first differs from the static rank-zero turn at its first action or only later. No new maps, training or policy evaluation.
interpretation: The first-action agreement metric is blind to roughly one third of this two-turn teacher's nonstatic whole-turn selections in the existing training data, and to more than one quarter in the existing validation data. Distinct completed-turn candidates can start with the same action and diverge later. This does not show that atomic behavioral cloning cannot learn such sequences: its later observations contain the intermediate states. It does show that first-action accuracy is an incomplete proxy for plan imitation. The analysis is post hoc on previously inspected two-turn teacher data, not evidence of terminal strength, three-turn teacher behavior, student improvement or Elo.
decision: Keep policies unchanged. Any plan-level distillation experiment must predeclare fresh disjoint training and game-gate maps, avoid using these old validation maps for tuning, and test complete both-seat games rather than only first-action agreement.
